reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 20. Nay or No: 19. Not Voting: 1. Of 39 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 39 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 207 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

A zip code should never determine a child’s ability to grow up healthy. 

Today, I celebrated the opening of  Arverne’s new Pediatric Dental Services, made possible in part by the $1.5 million in federal funding I secured. 

This investment will expand access to essential pediatric services and give kids and families the opportunity to receive high-quality care closer to home.

We will never forget the innocent lives we lost, the sacrifices of our nation's bravest heroes, and the painful memory we carry 25 years later. 

America was wounded, but even in our darkest moment—we prevailed because of our ability to come together as Americans with resiliency, compassion, and civic duty. 

We continue to honor those we lost, and the families who help us carry on their memory, now and forever.

The Trump DHS' latest attempt to pit Americans against one another is not only  bigoted but also entirely un-American. Sowing division doesn't make us stronger. It weakens our communities.
 
I stand in solidarity with the Sikh community and the thousands of Sikh neighbors, friends, and workers who call #NY05 home. You belong here.

Every NYC Mayor has attended 9/11 remembrance ceremonies to pay their respects to those we lost on September 11, 2001. Mayor Mamdani has the same right and should pay his respects and stand alongside New Yorkers as the city remembers. 
 
This is a moment when political differences are set aside to make room for unity. 

On the 25th anniversary of those devastating events, let us continue our solemn tradition of coming together to honor the survivors, the families of lost loved ones, and the courageous first responders who ran into unknown danger to save lives.

The American workforce is at the heart of our nation’s progress. Today, we recognize those workers and unions who drive our economy and help make #NY05 and our country stronger every day. 

Happy Labor Day! https://t.co/ZeIuEBYHHS

I appreciate all who participated in making our community stronger.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
